entrypoints.summary: An HTTP POST endpoint configured with extended URL-encoded body parsing accepts application/x-www-form-urlencoded request bodies.
urlencodedParser selects the extended qs parser when the extended option is not false and supplies the request body to that parser.

affected_components.role: The middleware selects the extended parser and queryparse calls qs with the infinite depth option.

causal_paths.kind: HTTP URL-encoded body to qs parsing configuration

code_slices.surrounding_context: The middleware selects extendedparser unless options.extended is explicitly false; queryparse first enforces parameterLimit and derives arrayLimit from the parameter count.
code_slices.vulnerable: extendedparser returns queryparse, which calls parse(body, { allowPrototypes: true, arrayLimit: arrayLimit, depth: Infinity, parameterLimit: parameterLimit }).

negative_controls: Compare against a non-malicious URL-encoded body accepted by the endpoint.
Do not use process termination as the expected positive marker; the audit did not find a server crash.
observability.positive_marker: Increased response elapsed time and delayed request-queue processing under crafted concurrent traffic.

preconditions: The target exposes an HTTP endpoint using bodyParser.urlencoded with extended parsing enabled.
The endpoint accepts application/x-www-form-urlencoded bodies and deployment request-size/concurrency conditions permit the crafted traffic.

trigger_steps.payload_shape: A URL-encoded request body with attacker-controlled nested parameter structure; the report PoC uses multiple threads.
trigger_steps.summary: Send concurrent HTTP POST requests with Content-Type application/x-www-form-urlencoded and attacker-constructed body data to the configured endpoint.

relation_candidates.rationale: The extended parser accepts the supplied body and passes it to qs with an infinite depth setting.
The audit states that unlimited nested parsing allows an untrusted user to make the server run slowly and control incoming-request processing time.
The report identifies request-queue slowdown as the most severe observed impact from crafted concurrent requests.
Excessive parsing time prevents legitimate requests from being processed in a timely manner.
The audit explains that a finite depth causes excess nested syntax to be treated as text; the report marks the finding fixed but does not provide the implementation patch.

impact.affected_asset: Availability and response timeliness of the application endpoint and its request-processing queue.
impact.attacker_capability: An unauthenticated remote client can submit concurrent crafted URL-encoded bodies that increase parsing time and delay other requests.
impact.security_effect: Denial of timely HTTP service through request-queue slowdown.

causal_trace.summary: A remote client supplies an application/x-www-form-urlencoded request body containing attacker-chosen nested parameter syntax to an endpoint using the extended parser.
The extended parser passes the body to qs with depth set to Infinity, so nested URL parameters have no maximum child-depth bound; finite-depth excess would instead be treated as plain text.

qs parses attacker-controlled nesting without an upper depth limit, allowing the client to control request-processing time; concurrent crafted requests consume processing before other queued requests are handled.
Legitimate requests can be delayed in the server request queue, resulting in denial of timely service. The audit explicitly reports queue slowdown and no server-crash technique.

failure.operation: Parse an attacker-controlled URL-encoded body through qs with depth: Infinity.

primary_invariant.kind: bounded parsing work / maximum nesting depth
primary_invariant.statement: Parsing untrusted URL-encoded nested parameters must enforce a finite maximum depth so deeper syntax is not recursively parsed without bound.
primary_invariant.violated_because: The reviewed extended-parser configuration invokes qs.parse with depth: Infinity.

quality.review_notes: The audit supplies a finding-level mechanism, a local HTTP PoC configuration and sender, and a reviewed immutable vulnerable source. The bundle contains no upstream remediation commit, release linkage, regression test, or independently preserved complete malicious-versus-benign timing output. “Fixed” is therefore recorded only as report status, not as a verified implementation detail. Applicability is conditioned on an endpoint accepting URL-encoded input through the extended parser and on request-size/concurrency conditions.

remediation.invariant_restored: The URL-encoded extended parser must apply a finite nesting-depth limit, causing syntax beyond that bound to remain plain text rather than being parsed as additional nested structure.
mitigation_classes: configurable depth bound for untrusted nested URL-encoded input

oracle.channel: HTTP response elapsed time under concurrent requests
oracle.expected_negative: A non-malicious URL-encoded body of an accepted size is processed without the malicious nested-input queue-slowdown behavior.
oracle.expected_positive: Concurrent crafted URL-encoded nested-input requests produce materially delayed responses or queue slowdown under the stated extended-parser configuration.
